Sourdough Starter Guide

A sourdough starter is a fermented mixture of flour and water that contains wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria. To create a starter, mix equal weights of whole wheat flour and water in a glass jar and leave it uncovered by a tight lid at room temperature.

Feeding Schedule

Discard all but fifty grams of the starter each day, then feed it with fifty grams of flour and fifty grams of water. A healthy starter doubles in volume within four to six hours after feeding and smells pleasantly tangy, like yogurt.

Troubleshooting

If the starter develops a layer of grey liquid called hooch, it is hungry. Pour off the hooch and feed it more often. Pink or orange streaks indicate contamination, and the starter must be thrown away. Keep the jar in the refrigerator if you bake only once a week, and feed it weekly.

Baking the Loaf

Mix five hundred grams of bread flour, three hundred and fifty grams of water, one hundred grams of active starter and ten grams of salt. Fold the dough every thirty minutes during the first two hours, then proof it overnight in the refrigerator. Bake in a preheated Dutch oven at 230 degrees Celsius for forty minutes.
